chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadala from Aban from Jamil said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When you perform Hajj on foot and throw the pebbles at the Jamarah, then the walking (for the purpose of the penalty) is concluded."

key_terms.الْجَمْرَةَ: The Jamarah (the pillar/stones used in stoning ritual)
key_terms.الْمَشْيُ: The walking (referring to the specific act of walking as a penalty)

ai.seo_question: What concludes the walking penalty for a pilgrim in Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific mechanism of expiation (kaffarah) for unintentional violations of Ihram conditions, linking the physical act of stoning the Jamarat with the required duration of walking. It highlights the jurisprudential principle that the completion of the ritual stoning while in motion serves as the definitive termination of the walking penalty, ensuring the pilgrim’s obligations are met without unnecessary burden. This ruling is particularly significant in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between intentional transgressions and accidental errors during the Hajj rites.
